subcommands.notes: Prompts for confirmation before removing the autoMode section from user settings; `-y`/`--yes` skips the prompt. Requires v2.1.212+.

subcommands.description: Manages the background-session supervisor.
subcommands.name: daemon
subcommands.notes: Hidden from top-level help; with piped input the bare command runs the supervisor in the foreground, and service install is disabled in this version. Carries the umbrella --json-path and --log-file options.

subcommands.description: Tails the background-session supervisor log.
subcommands.name: daemon logs
subcommands.notes: Hidden from top-level help; runs until interrupted.

subcommands.description: Runs the background-session supervisor in the foreground.
subcommands.name: daemon run
subcommands.notes: Hidden; takes an optional json-path positional; service install is disabled in this version, so the daemon runs on demand.

subcommands.description: Prints supervisor pid, version, uptime, and socket state.
subcommands.name: daemon status
subcommands.notes: Hidden; exits 1 when the supervisor is not running, which is a normal state.

subcommands.description: Shuts down the supervisor and terminates background sessions.
subcommands.name: daemon stop
subcommands.notes: Hidden; `--any` also stops a transient daemon and `--keep-workers` leaves detached sessions running.

subcommands.description: Removes the background service integration.
subcommands.name: daemon uninstall
subcommands.notes: Hidden; destructive to service registration.

subcommands.description: Prints read-only installation and settings diagnostics without starting a session.
subcommands.name: doctor
subcommands.notes: Ran to completion with exit 0 under piped stdout in 2.1.287, unlike the 2.1.200-era hang; reports install method, search, auto-update state, and settings validation errors. The fuller checkup is /doctor inside a session.

subcommands.description: Runs the enterprise auth and telemetry gateway server.
subcommands.name: gateway
subcommands.notes: Long-running; requires `--config` pointing at a gateway.yaml. Available since v2.1.195.

subcommands.description: Imports configuration from another coding agent.
subcommands.name: import
subcommands.notes: Documented (v2.1.213+) to start an interactive session running /import with codex, gemini, or cursor sources; in this 2.1.287 build the command prints `not yet available in this build` instead.

subcommands.description: Installs or reinstalls the native binary.
subcommands.name: install
subcommands.notes: Positional target accepts stable, latest, or a specific version; `--force` reinstalls even when installed.

subcommands.description: Prints a background session's recent terminal output.
subcommands.name: logs
subcommands.notes: Takes the short session id printed by `--bg`.

subcommands.description: Adds an MCP server to Claude Code configuration.
subcommands.name: mcp add
subcommands.notes: stdio servers take a command and args after `--`; HTTP/SSE servers take a URL. Transport is validated app-side and an invalid value is refused before any write.

subcommands.description: Imports MCP servers from Claude Desktop.
subcommands.name: mcp add-from-claude-desktop
subcommands.notes: Mac and WSL only.

subcommands.description: Adds an MCP server from a JSON string.
subcommands.name: mcp add-json
subcommands.notes: Supports stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket server definitions.

subcommands.description: Prints details about one configured MCP server.
subcommands.name: mcp get
subcommands.notes: Unapproved .mcp.json servers show as pending and are not connected to.

subcommands.description: Lists configured MCP servers with health checks.
subcommands.name: mcp list
subcommands.notes: Performs live network health checks, so timing depends on connectivity; text output only.

subcommands.description: Runs a configured MCP server's OAuth flow.
subcommands.name: mcp login
subcommands.notes: Opens a browser by default; `--no-browser` prints the authorization URL for SSH or headless use and asks for the redirect URL back at a prompt.

subcommands.description: Clears stored OAuth credentials for an MCP server.
subcommands.name: mcp logout
subcommands.notes: Mutates stored credentials.

subcommands.description: Removes an MCP server.
subcommands.name: mcp remove
subcommands.notes: Without `--scope`, removes from whichever scope the server exists in.

subcommands.description: Resets approvals for project-scoped .mcp.json servers.
subcommands.name: mcp reset-project-choices
subcommands.notes: Clears both approvals and rejections in this project.

subcommands.description: Starts the Claude Code MCP server.
subcommands.name: mcp serve
subcommands.notes: Long-running stdio server for another MCP client; accepts `--debug` and `--verbose`.

subcommands.description: Shows a plugin's options or saves values from stdin.
subcommands.name: plugin configure
subcommands.notes: Prints which options are unset; `--values-stdin` reads a JSON object so no prompt is needed; `--json` machine-reads the option list.

subcommands.description: Shows a plugin's component inventory and projected token cost.
subcommands.name: plugin details
subcommands.notes: Read-only.

subcommands.description: Disables an enabled plugin.
subcommands.name: plugin disable
subcommands.notes: Takes a plugin name or `-a`/`--all` for every enabled plugin; scope auto-detects unless `--scope` is given.

subcommands.description: Enables a disabled plugin.
subcommands.name: plugin enable
subcommands.notes: Scope auto-detects unless `--scope` is given.

subcommands.description: Runs a plugin's eval suite and reports scored results.
subcommands.name: plugin eval
subcommands.notes: Large operator flag surface (--mocks, --judge-model, --concurrency, --max-cost-usd, and more) not inventoried here; the first run in an untrusted plugin directory asks for confirmation unless `--trust-plugin` is passed; makes real model calls.

subcommands.description: Scaffolds a new plugin under ~/.claude/skills/.
subcommands.name: plugin init
subcommands.notes: Alias `new`; `--with` selects extra component scaffolds; auto-loads next session as <name>@skills-dir.

subcommands.description: Installs a plugin from a marketplace.
subcommands.name: plugin install
subcommands.notes: Alias `i`; a marketplace-declared command must be confirmed by a person, so `-y`/`--yes` (or a pinned `--accept-command` sha256) is required when stdin or stdout is not a TTY; `--json` prints one machine-readable result line.

subcommands.description: Lists installed plugins.
subcommands.name: plugin list
subcommands.notes: `--json` prints a JSON array; `--available` adds marketplace plugins and `--data-size` measures saved data, both requiring `--json`.

subcommands.description: Adds a marketplace from a URL, path, or GitHub repo.
subcommands.name: plugin marketplace add
subcommands.notes: `--claudeai` adds a claude.ai-hosted marketplace by name; `--sparse` limits checkout paths.

subcommands.description: Lists configured marketplaces.
subcommands.name: plugin marketplace list
subcommands.notes: `--json` prints machine-readable output.

subcommands.description: Removes a configured marketplace.
subcommands.name: plugin marketplace remove
subcommands.notes: Alias `rm`; without `--scope`, removes the declaration from every scope.

subcommands.description: Updates marketplace definitions from their source.
subcommands.name: plugin marketplace update
subcommands.notes: Updates all marketplaces when no name is given.

subcommands.description: Removes auto-installed plugin dependencies no longer needed.
subcommands.name: plugin prune
subcommands.notes: Alias `autoremove`; prompts for confirmation unless `-y`/`--yes`; `--dry-run` lists what would go.

subcommands.description: Creates a validated git tag for a plugin release.
subcommands.name: plugin tag
subcommands.notes: Validates that plugin.json and any enclosing marketplace entry agree; `--dry-run` previews and `--push` pushes to a remote.

subcommands.description: Runs a mod's TypeScript test suite.
subcommands.name: plugin test
subcommands.notes: Runs every *.test.ts and *.test.tsx under the directory in a child of this binary; exits 1 on failure.

subcommands.description: Uninstalls an installed plugin.
subcommands.name: plugin uninstall
subcommands.notes: Alias `remove`; `--keep-data` preserves the plugin's data directory; `--prune` also removes unneeded auto-installed dependencies but prompts, requiring `-y` in non-interactive contexts.

subcommands.description: Updates an installed plugin to its latest version.
subcommands.name: plugin update
subcommands.notes: Same marketplace-declared-command confirmation flow as install; `-y` or `--accept-command` answers it headlessly; restart required to apply.

subcommands.description: Validates a plugin or marketplace manifest.
subcommands.name: plugin validate
subcommands.notes: `--json` emits the validation report; `--strict` turns warnings into exit 1 for CI.

subcommands.description: Deletes all Claude Code state for a project.
subcommands.name: project purge
subcommands.notes: Prompts by default; `-y`/`--yes` skips, `-i`/`--interactive` confirms each item, `--dry-run` previews, `--all` purges every project and is mutually exclusive with a path.

subcommands.description: Starts a Remote Control server for claude.ai or the mobile app.
subcommands.name: remote-control
subcommands.notes: Hidden from top-level help; runs as a persistent server in the current directory and requires a subscribed Claude account; its own flag surface (--spawn, --capacity, --session-id, -c, --[no-]chrome) is documented in `claude remote-control --help` and not inventoried here; the root `--remote-control` flag is the interactive-session form.

subcommands.description: Restarts a background session with its conversation intact.
subcommands.name: respawn
subcommands.notes: Takes a session id or `--all` for every running session, for example to pick up an updated binary.

subcommands.description: Deletes a background session and its worktree.
subcommands.name: rm
subcommands.notes: Works on already-exited sessions; a refused removal prints the exact `--discard-unpushed <commit>@<worktree-id>` or `--force-remove-worktree <worktree-id>` value to re-run with; the transcript stays on disk.

subcommands.description: Registers this machine as a self-hosted cloud-session runner.
subcommands.name: self-hosted-runner
subcommands.notes: Hidden; long-running operator surface (v2.1.224+) with setup, doctor, and orchestrator subcommands and dozens of flags; see `claude self-hosted-runner --help`; not inventoried here.

subcommands.description: Generates a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts.
subcommands.name: setup-token
subcommands.notes: Requires a Claude subscription and prints a secret to the terminal without saving it; treat as an interactive secrets flow.

subcommands.description: Stops a background session while keeping it resumable.
subcommands.name: stop
subcommands.notes: Alias `kill`; the conversation is kept and reopens with `claude attach <id>`.

subcommands.description: Runs a cloud-hosted multi-agent code review and prints findings.
subcommands.name: ultrareview
subcommands.notes: Takes a PR number or base branch as target; exits 0 on success and 1 on failure; `--json` prints the raw payload, `--timeout` caps the wait (default 45 minutes), `--post` posts findings to a github.com PR.

subcommands.description: Checks for updates and installs if available.
subcommands.name: update
subcommands.notes: Alias `upgrade`; behavior depends on install method and channel; reports up-to-date for package-manager installs it cannot upgrade.

wrapper_notes: Use `claude -p` for non-interactive wrapper runs; plain `claude "query"` starts an interactive session seeded with the prompt. Piped stdout alone also selects the non-interactive input requirement even without -p, so a wrapper that captures stdout changes the CLI's behavior.

The parser is strict: an unrecognized long or short option exits 1 with `error: unknown option`, so Claudine must not forward switches it cannot classify, and a user argument that looks like an unknown switch genuinely fails rather than passing through.

Documentation can drift from the binary: `--exec` is documented in the CLI reference but rejected as unknown by the 2.1.287 parser, and `claude import` documents an interactive flow but prints `not yet available in this build`. Verify flags against the running binary, not the docs alone.

A variadic root switch (--add-dir, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --betas, --file, --mcp-config, --tools, --channels, --dangerously-load-development-channels) grabs the immediately following token unconditionally, even when it looks like an option, and keeps consuming non-option tokens. Never place another flag directly after a variadic switch in a mixed command line.

An optional-value root switch (--resume, --from-pr, --worktree, --teleport, --cloud, --remote-control, --prompt-suggestions) does not consume a following token that looks like an option, but does consume a plain one, which would steal a user's positional prompt.
The --debug filter binds only in the equals form; `--debug api` enables debug mode without filtering, so wrappers must emit --debug=api.

Invalid values fail at three different layers: commander choice validation exits at parse time (--output-format, --permission-mode, --input-format, --system-prompt-snapshot, --permission-prompts, --autocompact, --prompt-suggestions); app-level validation exits after parsing (--setting-sources, --session-id UUID, mcp add transport); and --effort only warns and falls back to the default.
`claude auth status` exits 1 when logged out and `claude daemon status` exits 1 when no supervisor runs; both are normal states, so parse stdout before classifying the exit as a crash.
`claude mcp list` performs live network health checks; expect slow or offline-sensitive runs.
`claude doctor` now completes without a TTY; the 2.1.200-era 20-second hang did not reproduce in 2.1.287, but a timeout guard is still cheap insurance.

Top-level help omits hidden commands (daemon, remote-control, self-hosted-runner) and hidden flags (--sdk-url, and docs-only flags like --max-turns, --init, --init-only, --maintenance, --advisor, --teammate-mode); help incompleteness is documented policy, so absence from help is not evidence a flag is unavailable.

--bg cannot be combined with -p and prints a session id that `claude attach`, `logs`, `stop`, and `rm` take; a leading --dangerously-skip-permissions or --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions routes `daemon <subcommand>` to the daemon command since v2.1.199.

Print mode skips the workspace trust dialog and silently ignores settings files that fail validation, so wrappers should only launch it in trusted directories and cannot rely on settings errors surfacing.
Native installs auto-update in the background (channel latest by default), so the binary a wrapper resolved can change between runs; the launcher is a symlink into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/.

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is the broadest public isolation knob, moving settings, session history, and plugins together; --bare is stronger but restricts auth to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper, never reading OAuth or keychain credentials.
On Windows without Git for Windows the shell tool is PowerShell; with it, Bash via Git Bash; CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH points at bash.exe when discovery fails.
--settings values override settings files for the session but managed policy still wins; --restricted ignores user, project, and local settings entirely.

System-prompt flags (--system-prompt, --system-prompt-file, --append-system-prompt, --append-system-prompt-file, --system-prompt-snapshot, --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections, and the subagent variants) work in both interactive and non-interactive modes; this topic records their spellings and value shapes only, with semantics in the system-prompt topic.

agent-logging.reason: On-disk transcripts are a DISTINCT format from the stream-json SDK events and carry interactive-only types Claude's JSONL ingestion does not model (mode, permission-mode, ai-title, last-prompt, queue-operation, and 16 attachment subtypes incl. task_reminder/diagnostics/command_permissions). history.jsonl uses {project, timestamp(unix ms)} with NO session_id — any Claudine history parsing keyed on session_id must be corrected. sessions/{pid}.json gained live fields (status, name, peerProtocol, updatedAt) useful for live monitoring. There is NO native SQLite log, so Claudine's own JSONL->SQLite metrics layer remains the only structured index; Claudine must not look for a native log database.

record_types.discriminator: (no type discriminator — fixed schema per line)
log level token in line prefix

surfaces.naming: {session_id}.jsonl under sanitized-cwd dir (path separators -> '-')
surfaces.notes: Primary interactive audit trail. Append-only JSONL, never rotated/archived by Claude. Sharded by sanitized cwd, NOT by date. Assistant events carry usage/cost in message.usage; there is NO top-level 'result' event in the transcript (that is stream-json only). First line is usually a 'mode' event.

surfaces.naming: agent-{agent_id}.jsonl; session_id is a DIRECTORY (not file) when subagents exist
surfaces.notes: Same JSONL schema as the parent transcript but every line carries isSidechain:true + agentId + promptId. The {session_id} path segment is a directory alongside the {session_id}.jsonl file.

surfaces.naming: history.jsonl (single append-only file)
surfaces.notes: One record per user prompt: {display, pastedContents, timestamp(unix ms), project(literal cwd)}. NO session_id field. Observed file grew to ~6 MB.

surfaces.naming: {pid}.json (one file per live process; created at start, removed on clean exit)
surfaces.notes: Live session registry. Fields observed: pid, sessionId, cwd, startedAt(ms), procStart(local date string), version, peerProtocol, kind(interactive|headless), entrypoint(cli|ide|web), name, nameSource, status(idle|active|busy|error), updatedAt(ms), statusUpdatedAt(ms).

surfaces.naming: {file_hash}@v{n} snapshots under session_id dir
surfaces.notes: File-content snapshots for undo/file-history. ~370 session dirs observed. State store, not a log; included because transcript file-history-snapshot events reference it.

surfaces.naming: n/a (in-memory payload, refreshed ~1s)
surfaces.notes: Claude pipes a live JSON object (session_id, model, cwd, cost, context %, tokens, git) to the configured statusLine.command. NOT a Claude-written file. The observed ~/.claude/statusline.log (396 MB here) is generated by the USER's statusline script (cc-statusline), not by Claude Code itself.
surfaces.path_macos: stdin JSON to statusLine.command (configured in settings.json)

surfaces.naming: per-subsystem .log files (main.log, mcp.log, mcp-server-*.log, sdk_daemon.log, etc.)
surfaces.notes: Desktop (Electron) app logs ONLY. Plain text with ISO timestamps + [level]. Per-MCP-server logs (mcp-server-{Name}.log). Do NOT contain conversation content or tool calls. Separate dir + format from CLI.

surfaces.naming: empty scratch dir per session_id (~770 observed, all empty post-cleanup)
surfaces.notes: Per-session scratch/mount directories. Observed empty; transient.

surfaces.naming: {task_id}/ containing .lock (0 bytes) + .highwatermark (1 byte)
surfaces.notes: Background Task tool state. .lock is an advisory lock held while the task runs (live-locked). ~71 task dirs observed.

surfaces.naming: snapshot-zsh-{epoch_nanos}-{rand}.sh
surfaces.notes: Shell-environment capture scripts for session restoration (env vars, aliases). State, not logs.

surfaces.naming: info.json (hardware cache), stats-cache.json (usage stats), .last-update-result.json (auto-update outcome)
surfaces.notes: Misc global JSON state. .last-update-result.json carries version_from/version_to + ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.

changes: Corrected the local-model claim: Ollama, oMLX, LM Studio, llama.cpp (b7187+), and vLLM serve the Anthropic Messages API natively, so a direct ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL override works without a translating gateway; a gateway is required only for OpenAI-only endpoints.
Removed the custom_models frontmatter block — user-side model extension belongs solely to the model-config topic.

default_models.notes: Most capable model; long autonomous sessions. NOT the default on any account type — selected only via /model fable, the `best` alias (where Fable 5 is accessible), or a model setting. Safety-classifier flagged requests auto-fallback to Opus.
Latest Opus. On the Anthropic API the `default` special value resolves here (also Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go). Always 1M window on the API. 1M window elsewhere is plan-dependent.
Opus 4.7. Default model on Claude Platform on AWS (`default` resolves here). Default effort is xhigh.
Opus 4.6; `opus` resolves here on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry. Supports 1M window; supports the fixed-thinking-budget mode (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING).

Latest Sonnet. Default on Pro, Team Standard, and Enterprise subscription seats (`default` resolves here). On the Anthropic API always runs with the native 1M window — no 200K variant and no [1m] suffix. Requires Claude Code v2.1.197+.
Sonnet 4.6; `sonnet` resolves here on Claude Platform on AWS. 1M window requires usage credits on most plans.
Sonnet 4.5; `sonnet` resolves here on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry (`default` resolves here on those providers).
Fast/efficient model. Used for background functionality and the `haiku` alias. Legacy alias ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL maps here (deprecated in favor of ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL).

dynamic_listing.example: Interactive only: run `claude` then `/model`. Non-interactive consumers must read the resolved model from the stream-json `result.modelUsage` field rather than enumerate the catalog.
dynamic_listing.method: none — no `claude models` / `--list-models` subcommand or model-catalog API. The /model picker is interactive-only (requires a TTY) and is the sole native catalog view. Gateway discovery (/v1/models) populates that same interactive picker, not a programmatic listing.

model_selection.notes: Switch model at runtime. `/model` (no arg) opens the picker; `/model <alias|name>` switches immediately. As of v2.1.153, Enter saves the choice as the default for new sessions (writes `model` in user settings); `s` switches for this session only. Highest-precedence at runtime within an open session.
Toggles fast mode (implicit Opus switch); refused when the resulting model is outside `availableModels`.
Sets adaptive-reasoning effort (low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultracode), not the model itself, but part of the model-behavior surface. Also adjustable via the effort slider inside `/model`.
Toggles extended thinking default (`alwaysThinkingEnabled`) and the Fable-5 auto-fallback switch ('switch models when a message is flagged').
Sets the model for the launched session only. Accepts an alias (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable/best/default) or a full model name. Overrides the `model` setting and ANTHROPIC_MODEL for this session.
Comma-separated fallback chain tried in order when the primary is overloaded/unavailable (max 3 after dedup). Overrides the `fallbackModel` setting for the session.
Enables the server-side advisor tool with a model alias/id for the session. Takes precedence over the `advisorModel` setting. v2.1.98+.
Sets effort for the session; overrides `effortLevel` setting, does not persist.
Path or inline JSON whose keys (e.g. model, availableModels, modelOverrides, fallbackModel, effortLevel, advisorModel) override the same keys in settings.json files for this session.
Inline JSON defining subagents dynamically; each may carry a `model` field (subagent frontmatter shape).
Sets the model for the launched session only (same scope rule as --model). Lower precedence than --model.

Pins what each alias resolves to (full model name / provider ID). Also drives opusplan phase resolution and, on third-party providers, Fable-5 fallback identification. As of v2.1.195, an OPUS-family var also overrides the model restored on resume.
Model for ALL subagents and agent teams. Overrides the Agent tool's `model` parameter and subagent frontmatter `model`. Set to `inherit` for normal resolution.
Adds one custom entry to the /model picker (no validation of the ID). Pairs with ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME / _DESCRIPTION. For gateway-routed models when discovery is off.
Populates the /model picker from the gateway GET /v1/models endpoint (Anthropic Messages format only); results cached to ~/.claude/cache/gateway-models.json. v2.1.129+.
Selects the wire/API format (Bedrock InvokeModel, Agent Platform rawPredict, Anthropic Messages for Foundry) and the provider-form model IDs the aliases resolve to.

settings.json key (user ~/.claude/settings.json, project .claude/settings.json, or managed). Sets the initial model at startup; users can still pick Default in /model unless enforceAvailableModels redirects it.

Managed/policy allowlist restricting every model-selection surface (main model, aliases, fast mode, subagents, skills/commands, advisor, background agent). Family wildcard, version prefix, or full ID.
Extends the availableModels allowlist to the Default option so Default cannot resolve outside the list. v2.1.175+.
Persistent fallback chain (array); overridden by --fallback-model.

Maps Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific strings (Bedrock ARN, Vertex version name, Foundry deployment). Used by /model picker entries; does not transform values passed directly via ANTHROPIC_MODEL/--model/ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL.
Persistence for effort, the advisor model, and the extended-thinking default respectively.

The actual model ID sent on each inference request after alias resolution. Bedrock uses {model} in the path; Agent Platform uses the publisher model path. modelOverrides may rewrite the built-in ID here.

Headless/stream-json output reports per-model usage in the terminal result event — the authoritative way to read the resolved model(s) in non-interactive mode (the retirement/deprecation stderr warning is suppressed for json/stream-json).

agent-models.precedence: interactive_command (/model, runtime) > cli_flag (--model) > env_var (ANTHROPIC_MODEL) > config_file (model setting); config_file layering is managed > project > user. --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL apply to the launched session only. Resumed sessions (--resume/--continue) restore the transcript's saved model unless retired/excluded, but a launch-time --model/ANTHROPIC_MODEL (and, v2.1.195+, an ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL-family var) overrides the restored model. Organization restrictions and availableModels are enforced on top of every surface.
agent-models.reason: Claudine's `model_catalog` module maintains a merged provider model catalog with static Claude entries and alias resolution plus user overrides. The Claude lineup and selection surface have shifted substantially and the static catalog / alias map for the Claude provider needs refreshing: Fable 5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and the new aliases (`best`, `fable`, `sonnet[1m]`, `opus[1m]`, `opusplan`) plus the account-dependent `default` resolver; new selection surfaces Claudine's Claude wrapper does not yet model — fallback chains (--fallback-model / fallbackModel), the advisor (--advisor / advisorModel), effort levels (--effort / effortLevel / CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL), ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION, gateway model discovery (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY + ~/.claude/cache/gateway-models.json), modelOverrides, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=inherit. To accurately merge/override and report Claude models, Claudine needs a catalog refresh and awareness of these surfaces.

api_standards.notes: Primary path for user-added arbitrary models. Claude Code emits the Anthropic Messages API to this base URL. Cloud-provider deployments (Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS) use their own base-url variables and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* toggles but are intended for Claude-family models, not generic user models.

changes: Local runners (Ollama, oMLX, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) are now supported paths via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL because they expose Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoints; the previous revision incorrectly classified them as unsupported/gateway-required.
Ollama and oMLX ship first-class `launch claude` integration hooks in addition to the base-URL override path.
Claude Code settings precedence clarified as managed > CLI arguments > local > project > user.
Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL_{NAME,DESCRIPTION,SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES} variables, which were not present in the prior revision.
Confirmed that gateway model discovery only adds IDs prefixed with `claude` or `anthropic`, and that discovered explicit IDs fold into built-in alias rows when they resolve to the same model.

cloud_bridge.mechanism: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at an Anthropic-Messages-compatible gateway or proxy

model-config.default_model_site: Top-level `model` key in ~/.claude/settings.json (or project/local/managed settings.json); session-scope override via ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var or --model flag; precedence is --model > ANTHROPIC_MODEL > settings.json `model`.

env_vars.effect: Redirects the Anthropic Messages API endpoint to a gateway, proxy, or local runner. Changes where requests go, not which model answers.
env_vars.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL

env_vars.effect: Sets the active model for the launched session. Lower precedence than --model, higher than the settings.json `model` key.
env_vars.name: ANTHROPIC_MODEL

env_vars.effect: API key sent as `x-api-key`. Overrides a saved claude.ai login when set.
env_vars.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

env_vars.effect: Bearer token sent in the `Authorization` header. Preferred for gateway and local-runner authentication.
env_vars.name: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN

env_vars.effect: Pins what the `fable` alias resolves to and identifies Fable 5 for automatic fallback on third-party providers.
env_vars.name: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL

local_runners.example: ollama launch claude  # or manually: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama claude --model qwen3:1.7b
local_runners.notes: Ollama serves an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint and ships a native `ollama launch claude` hook. Size/quantization tags such as `:1.7b` are part of the model identifier.

local_runners.example: omlx launch claude  # or manually: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<key> claude --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ6
local_runners.notes: oMLX serves an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint and ships a native `omlx launch claude` hook. Default port is 8000.
LM Studio serves an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint. Set auth token to `lmstudio` when authentication is disabled, or to the configured API token when required.
llama-server serves an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint (added in build b7187). The model ID is the `--alias` value or the GGUF filename.
vLLM serves an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint (v0.11.1+). Each vLLM process hosts one model; use `--served-model-name` aliases if needed.

Any local runner that exposes an Anthropic Messages API-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint can be pointed at directly. Runners that speak only the OpenAI Chat Completions API require a translating gateway.

quirks: The recommended stream is NDJSON on stdout, but the schema authority is the Agent SDK TypeScript declaration, not a standalone stream JSON Schema.
system/init is usually first, but synchronous plugin installation can emit system/plugin_install before init.
prompt_suggestion can arrive after result, so a parser should not treat every post-result record as impossible when that flag is enabled.
system/thinking_tokens is progress telemetry, not billable token usage.
Permission denials can appear both as system/permission_denied and final result.permission_denials; join by tool_use_id.
File changes are not a single provider-wide file_change event family; infer them from Edit/Write tool outputs, hooks, and diffs.
Model identity can be split across requested/init model, result.modelUsage keys, and model-refusal fallback events.
non-interactive-sessions.reason: Current Claude Code stream-json exposes newer event families and fields such as system/permission_denied, rate_limit_event, auth_status, prompt_suggestion, system/thinking_tokens, and model-refusal fallback that Claudine metadata and parsers should verify against.

schema_sources.notes: Official TypeScript Agent SDK reference documents query() as AsyncGenerator<SDKMessage> and defines stream message unions.
Local inspection of package/sdk.d.ts from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.200 is the strongest schema evidence for Claude Code 2.1.200.
Official headless docs describe print mode, JSON modes, stream-json framing, system/api_retry, system/init, and plugin install records.
Documents real-time SDK streaming behavior and the limitation that structured_output appears only in the final ResultMessage.
Defines CLI flags that select print mode, output format, input format, partial messages, hook events, permissions, budgets, model, and resume.

stream_contract.unknown_event_policy: Skip unknown type/subtype after recording the raw event at trace/debug; the SDKMessage union expands over time.

hitl_resume.answer_injection: Resume the same session_id with claude -p --resume <session-id> or SDK query({ options: { resume } }) after the wrapper has collected input. For SDK live sessions, reinitialize() after a transport gap redispatches pending permission requests to canUseTool.
hitl_resume.limitations: Defer is documented for -p / SDK workflows, not ordinary interactive terminal prompts. Prompt-tool approval cannot approve MCP tools marked as requiring user interaction as of v2.1.199. Wrapper callbacks must be idempotent because requests can be redispatched after reconnect.
hitl_resume.question_capture: In non-interactive mode, a PreToolUse hook can return permissionDecision defer. SDK/print results expose stop_reason tool_deferred and deferred_tool_use with the pending tool id, name, and input. Hooks and status-line inputs also provide session_id and transcript_path.

interruption_recovery.limitations: Transcripts are written continuously, so completed turns and recorded tool results survive terminal exit, Ctrl+C, crash, and process kill. Recovery of a tool call depends on it having been recorded or deferred before interruption. Simultaneously resuming the same session in two terminals is unsafe for automation because messages interleave into one transcript.

discovery.enable_disable: Per-skill: `disable-model-invocation: true` blocks the model from auto-invoking and preloading into subagents; `user-invocable: false` hides it from the `/` menu; `skillOverrides` can set a skill to `on`, `name-only`, `user-invocable-only`, or `off`. Global toggles: `--disable-slash-commands` disables all skills/commands for the session; `--bare` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` and `--safe-mode` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` skip skill discovery; `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS` disables only bundled skills; `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_POLICY_SKILLS` skips managed skills.
discovery.mechanism: File-system watcher scans managed, user, project, nested project, and --add-dir `.claude/skills/` directories at startup and watches them for changes. Skills are loaded progressively: `name`/`description` metadata is always in context; the full body loads when the skill is invoked by the user (`/skill-name`) or by the model (unless `disable-model-invocation: true`). Legacy `.claude/commands/*.md` are discovered the same way. Creating a top-level skills directory that did not exist when the session started requires a restart so the new directory can be watched.
discovery.notes: Plugin skills are managed through `/plugin` and are not affected by `skillOverrides`. Live change detection covers `SKILL.md` text only; plugin-side `hooks/`, `.mcp.json`, `agents/`, and `output-styles/` require `/reload-plugins`. Project skills require workspace trust before permission-related frontmatter such as `allowed-tools` takes effect.
discovery.precedence: Enterprise/managed > personal (`~/.claude/skills/`) > project (`.claude/skills/`) > plugin (namespaced). A user/project skill with the same name as a bundled skill overrides the bundled version. Nested project skills with clashing names are qualified by subdirectory path, e.g. `apps/web:deploy`, and the variant matching the working files is preferred. `skillOverrides` in settings can demote or hide a skill regardless of scope.

auth_setup.headless_notes: For headless operation, set `CODEX_API_KEY` (preferred) or `OPENAI_API_KEY` so the adapter can authenticate without a browser. Set `NO_BROWSER=1` to remove the `chat-gpt` method from the advertised list. Seed `~/.codex/auth.json` from a machine that completed ChatGPT login if running in a headless environment without API keys.
mechanisms: API key via methodId: api-key and _meta[api-key].apiKey
auth_setup.notes: Adapter reads auth from `~/.codex/auth.json` via the bundled Codex runtime. ChatGPT tokens auto-refresh; corrupted `auth.json` triggers automatic logout (LLM-28118 fix).

capabilities.notes: Standard ACP `initialize` handshake with `ProtocolVersion` (1), `ClientCapabilities`, `Implementation`, and `authMethods`. Adapter emits `agentInfo` with `name: "@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp"`, `title: "Codex"`, `version: "1.1.0"` (from the bundled package.json).

Three advertised auth methods: `api-key` (always), `chat-gpt` (unless `NO_BROWSER=1`), and `gateway` (only when client opts in via `clientCapabilities.auth._meta.gateway === true`). API key is supplied via `_meta["api-key"].apiKey` in the `AuthenticateRequest`.

`session/new` creates a conversation session tied to a working directory. Accepts optional `additionalDirectories` (absolute paths) and `mcpServers`. Response includes initial `models`, `modes`, and `configOptions` (mode, model, reasoning effort, and fast-mode toggle when supported by the chosen model).
`session/load` resumes an existing session by id. Capability advertised (`loadSession: true`). Streams the conversation history back as `session/update` notifications before the response.

`session/prompt` is the primary turn-taking method. `prompt` is `ContentBlock[]`; the adapter advertises `promptCapabilities.embeddedContext: true` and `promptCapabilities.image: true`. Cancellation is supported via the request signal.

`session/cancel` is a notification that stops the current turn. Adapter also handles protocol-level `$/cancel_request` (forwarded to the request signal) so any in-flight request to the adapter can be aborted.

Three modes: `read-only` (requires approval to edit/run), `agent` (workspace write, no network), and `agent-full-access` (danger-full-access, network on). Initial mode configurable via `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` env var. Switch with `session/set_mode`; agent emits `current_mode_update` notifications.

`session/update` notifications stream text, thoughts, tool calls, plan, mode, commands, and config-option changes. Adapter also streams tool progress, file changes, MCP tool calls, terminal output, web search, image generation, image view, token usage, and review events.

Reverse request `session/request_permission` is used for command execution, file change, MCP elicitation, and permissions-profile approvals. Approval options include `allow_once`/`allow_always`/`reject_once` plus Codex-specific decisions such as execpolicy amendment and network policy amendment.

The adapter does not register an `fs/read_text_file` handler. Filesystem reads happen inside the Codex App Server process via Codex's own tools. Clients advertising `fs.readTextFile: true` will not see reverse requests from this adapter.
Same as fs_read — writes go through Codex's built-in tools, not via `fs/write_text_file` reverse requests.

The adapter does not register `terminal/*` handlers. Commands run inside the Codex App Server and surface as tool calls (`kind: "execute"`) with streamed progress. Output bytes are carried in `_meta.terminal_output_delta` (default) or `_meta.terminal_output` (when client opts in via `clientCapabilities._meta.terminal_output: true`).

`mcpCapabilities.http: true`, `acp: false`, `sse: false`. Clients may pass HTTP-transport MCP servers in `session/new` (`mcpServers`) and Codex will manage them. SSE and ACP-protocol MCP servers are not exposed through the adapter. Codex-side MCP servers (managed via `codex mcp`) remain accessible through Codex's own tool surface.
Images are accepted in `promptCapabilities.image`. Image generation and image view surface as `tool_call`/`tool_call_update` events via `session/update`.
Adapter emits `plan` events as `session/update` notifications. Plan items from thread history are replayed on `session/load`.

Adapter registers three extension methods: `authentication/status`, `authentication/logout`, and the legacy `session/set_model`. `_meta` fields are used to carry Codex-specific data (e.g. `codex` approval params, `is_mcp_tool_approval`, `terminal_output_delta`).

changes: Verified `codex` CLI 0.142.5 has no native ACP entry point; recorded exact error strings for `codex --acp` and `codex acp`.
Corrected the auth method catalog: prior research listed `chatgpt`, `codex-api-key`, `openai-api-key`. The current adapter advertises `api-key`, `chat-gpt`, and `gateway` (capability-gated).

gaps: No official OpenAI-maintained ACP adapter; the canonical adapter is maintained by the ACP org. The legacy `@zed-industries/codex-acp` package is deprecated.
Empirical MCP-over-ACP behavior beyond the `http: true` capability is not formally documented outside the adapter source.
Codex-specific extension methods (`authentication/status`, `authentication/logout`, `session/set_model`) are documented only in the adapter source; they are not part of the published ACP spec.
Tool call payload formats for Codex-specific kinds (collab agent, web search, image generation, image view) are not formally documented; clients must consume them from the adapter source.

launch_modes.notes: Current recommended adapter (v1.1.0, 2026-07-02). Spawns the bundled Codex App Server over a private JSON-RPC channel and translates ACP JSON-RPC to/from it. Stderr is reserved for adapter/Codex logs; stdout carries newline-delimited JSON-RPC. Adapter name resolves at runtime to the value of `acp.agent({name})` — the agent advertises `name: "@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp", title: "Codex"`.

Legacy Zed-maintained adapter. npm description: "DEPRECATED — This package has been replaced by @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp." Last published 2026-06-08. The Zed repo's `main` branch remains accessible but has no tags after v0.16.0.

The main Codex CLI binary (v0.142.5 installed locally) has no native ACP mode. Direct probes on 0.142.5: `codex --acp` → "unexpected argument '--acp'"; `codex acp` → "unrecognized subcommand 'acp'". `codex app-server --listen stdio://` exposes the Codex App Server protocol, but that is a separate JSONL protocol, not ACP, and the adapter speaks it over a private channel rather than via the CLI's stdio surface.

permission_model.default_policy: no default; every approval request must receive a Selected or Cancelled response
permission_model.notes: Codex approval flows are richer than the generic ACP surface. Beyond allow/reject choices, the adapter may include Codex-specific decisions via `_meta.codex` on the option (execpolicy amendment, network policy amendment, root-grant, MCP tool-call approval with persist scope). Clients may either surface those to the user as raw options or render them as plain allow/reject buttons. On `session/cancel` or protocol-level `$/cancel_request`, the adapter propagates the abort signal to in-flight permission requests.

quirks: Codex CLI has no native ACP mode. Direct probes on the installed `codex-cli 0.142.5`: `codex --acp` returns "unexpected argument '--acp'"; `codex acp` returns "unrecognized subcommand 'acp'". The only protocol-mode subcommand is `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, which speaks the Codex App Server protocol (not ACP) and is what the adapter uses internally over a private stdio channel.

Auth method names changed between the legacy Zed adapter and the current ACP-org adapter. The legacy docs used `chatgpt`, `codex-api-key`, and `openai-api-key`; the current adapter advertises `api-key`, `chat-gpt`, and `gateway`. `api-key` is supplied via `_meta["api-key"].apiKey` and the adapter picks up the value from `CODEX_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` env vars if set.

`gateway` auth is capability-gated: it appears in `authMethods` only when the client opts in by sending `clientCapabilities.auth._meta.gateway: true` in `initialize`. It uses `_meta["gateway"]` with `baseUrl`, `headers`, and optional `providerName`.

`mcpCapabilities.acp: false` and `mcpCapabilities.sse: false` — the adapter only honours HTTP-transport MCP servers passed via `session/new`. SSE and ACP-transport MCP servers are not exposed through this adapter.

Fast mode is conditional: `createFastModeConfigOption` only emits the `fast-mode` config option when `modelSupportsFast` returns true for the current model. Clients may see Fast mode appear or disappear as the active model changes.

JetBrains 2026.1 clients have session config options intentionally disabled (`isSessionConfigEnabled()` returns false for `clientInfo.name === ...`), so `SessionConfigOption` payloads are absent for that client class until the upstream issue (LLM-28118) is resolved.

Corrupted `~/.codex/auth.json` triggers an automatic logout via `codexAcpClient.logout()`. The next request that needs auth fails with `RequestError.authRequired()` unless `DEFAULT_AUTH_REQUEST` is set.

The adapter bundles `@openai/codex ^0.142.5` by default; if a client wants a different Codex binary, set `CODEX_PATH`. The bundled version is intentionally pinned — versions other than the one specified in `package.json` may not be compatible.
The adapter enforces a 2-second grace period between stdin close and `codex` SIGKILL: if stdin closes, the adapter closes the Codex process' stdin, then kills it after 2s if it has not exited.
Stderr is reserved for adapter/Codex logs (2 KB rolling tail retained for crash diagnostics). Clients should never write to the adapter's stderr.
`INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` env var is honoured only at session creation; it does not retroactively change the mode of an existing session.
acp.reason: Codex CLI ACP support is adapter-based and continues to evolve on a separate cadence from the underlying Codex CLI. To wire Codex into Claudine's lifecycle pipeline over ACP, Claudine needs launch-mode detection for both `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` and the deprecated `@zed-industries/codex-acp`; capability negotiation that includes session config options (mode, model, reasoning effort, fast mode) and HTTP-only MCP; reverse-request routing for the single reverse request the adapter actually issues (`session/request_permission` with Codex-specific approval options like execpolicy and network policy amendments); permission policy integration for the three Codex modes (`read-only`, `agent`, `agent-full-access`); and headless auth detection (API key vs ChatGPT OAuth vs custom gateway).

wrapper_notes: Codex CLI 0.159.3 was installed and run on macOS arm64; Linux and Windows behavior comes from install scripts and documentation only.

--image/-i is greedy at the root, exec, and debug prompt-input: "codex exec -i a.png b.png" treats b.png as a second image and then waits on stdin for a prompt. Write --image=PATH or -iPATH, put the prompt before the switch, or end the switches with "--". At exec resume and exec fork the space form takes one value.

Codex reads the prompt from stdin when the argument is omitted or is "-", and when both exist appends stdin as a <stdin> block. Give it a closed stdin or a real prompt; with nothing available it prints "No prompt provided via stdin." and exits 1.

Non-global exec switches (--sandbox, --cd, --color, --oss, --profile, --add-dir) are not accepted after resume, fork, or review. Place them before the subcommand; the source merges the exec-level values into the subcommand. Only --model, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, --worktree, and the exec globals (--json, --output-schema, --output-last-message, --ephemeral, --skip-git-repo-check, --ignore-user-config, --ignore-rules, --thread-source, --strict-config) apply after it. Source-derived, not run, because a run would be billed.

exec has no --ask-for-approval; the interactive root has. A non-interactive run reports "approval: never" and takes its policy from configuration, so pass -c approval_policy=... when a different policy is needed.

An unauthenticated exec still prints its banner (workdir, model, sandbox, session id) on stderr, retries a websocket, and exits 101 on 401. exec resume with an unknown session operand did not fail a lookup before the network step, while exec fork failed immediately with "Session not found"; check the id yourself before resuming.

Parse errors exit 2 with a message naming the switch. Runtime errors for -c without "=" or an unknown --enable name exit 1. doctor --json and login status exit 1 on a failed check or missing login, so read the output rather than only the status.

A first word that is not a subcommand is taken as the interactive PROMPT: "codex mcp-server --help" printed the root help rather than an error. The mcp-server command from earlier versions no longer exists. A typo therefore starts a terminal UI instead of failing.

-c values are TOML first and a literal string second, so -c model=o3 and -c model="o3" both work but -c key=[a,b] needs quoting for the shell. Root-level -c values are lower precedence than the subcommand's.

--ephemeral and --ignore-user-config change what is read or written but authentication still comes from CODEX_HOME. Pointing CODEX_HOME at a fresh directory removes the login and creates a skills/.system folder there.

Hidden commands exist outside help output: execpolicy, tcp-tunnel, responses-api-proxy, stdio-to-uds, and debug trace-reduce and clear-memories. --yolo, --not-so-yolo, and --experimental-json are hidden aliases; none are documented as stable.
The developers.openai.com/codex pages now answer 308 redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs; use the new locations.

changes: NEW top-level envelope type `compacted` observed (73 occurrences): co-emitted with an event_msg `context_compacted` marker on each context compaction; its payload carries `message` + `replacement_history[]` (the post-compaction message stack). Prior research listed only session_meta/turn_context/response_item/event_msg.

Many new event_msg payload types observed in real rollouts: `exec_command_end` (shell-command completion with call_id/process_id/command[]/cwd/parsed_cmd[]), `agent_reasoning` (commentary-channel text), `context_compacted`, `thread_rolled_back` (num_turns), `entered_review_mode`/`exited_review_mode`, `collab_waiting_end`/`collab_agent_spawn_end`/`collab_close_end`/`collab_agent_interaction_end` (multi-agent collaboration — spawn carries new_thread_id/new_agent_nickname/new_agent_role/prompt), `error` (message + `codex_error_info` discriminator e.g. usage_limit_exceeded), `thread_name_updated`, `item_completed`. Prior research listed only 8 event_msg types.
NEW response_item payload type `ghost_snapshot` (git ghost-commit snapshot {ghost_commit:{id,parent,preexisting_untracked_files[],preexisting_untracked_dirs[]}}) backing undo/rollback.
`token_count.rate_limits` gained a `credits` sub-object {has_credits, unlimited, balance} alongside the existing primary/secondary windows + resets_at + plan_type.

Codex HOOKS are now a full 10-event lifecycle system (SessionStart, SubagentStart, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop, Stop) with stdin-JSON / stdout-JSON decision shapes and matcher regex — parity with Claude Code. Prior research described only a single coarse `notify` (AfterAgent) hook. This is a major adapter-relevant change.

NEW app-server/desktop surface `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` (inbox_items + automations with RRULE scheduling + automation_runs). Corresponds to the documented App Server / Automations / Inbox features.

Desktop (Electron) app logs confirmed at `~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/codex-desktop-{agentRunId}-{pid}-t{threadIdx}-i{instanceIdx}-{HHMMSS}-{n}.log`: date-sharded, per-process, JS-logger text format (`ISO-Z level [context] msg key=value`) — NOT Rust tracing, separate dir + format from CLI.
NEW separate `update-check.json` surface ({lastUpdateCheck} as HTTP RFC-1123 date) distinct from `version.json` ({latest_version,last_checked_at,dismissed_version}).

session_meta payload gains `parent_thread_id`, `multi_agent_version` (e.g. v1), and a structured `git` object {commit_hash, branch, repository_url}. Subagent sessions set `thread_source: subagent` and `source.subagent.thread_spawn` {parent_thread_id, depth, agent_path, agent_nickname, agent_role}.

logs_2.sqlite observed: ~147 MB / 10917 rows; observed levels TRACE/DEBUG/INFO/WARN only (no ERROR rows in this DB). New tracing targets observed: `codex_app_server::*`, `codex_models_manager::*`, `codex_core_skills::*`, `codex_core_plugins::*`, `codex_mcp::connection_manager`, `codex_otel::metrics::client`, `codex_rollout::*`.

default_models.notes: Newest frontier model; the documented starting point (`For most tasks in Codex, start with gpt-5.5`). When no model is configured, Codex defaults to the current recommended model, which is gpt-5.5. Available with ChatGPT or API-key auth; strongest for complex coding, computer use, knowledge work, and research.
Flagship frontier model for professional work (strong coding, reasoning, tool use, agentic workflows). Available with ChatGPT or API-key auth.
Fast, efficient mini model for responsive coding tasks and subagents. Lower-cost option for lighter work.
Text-only research preview model optimized for near-instant, real-time coding iteration. ChatGPT Pro subscribers only; no image input.

dynamic_listing.method: codex debug models [--bundled]  — prints the raw model catalog Codex sees as JSON. `--bundled` skips the remote refresh and prints only the catalog compiled into the current Codex binary. Complemented at runtime by `/status` (resolved model) and `/debug-config` (effective config layers).

model_selection.notes: Switch the active model (and reasoning effort, when available) during an interactive thread. `/model` opens the picker; selecting a model confirms it in the transcript. Verify with `/status`. Highest-precedence at runtime within an open session.
Toggle the model's Fast service tier (`on` / `off` / `status`) for the current thread when the active model advertises one; catalog-driven, so it is hidden for models without a Fast tier.
Read-only inspection of the active model, approval policy, writable roots, and remaining context. Not a selector, but the in-session way to confirm the resolved model.
Prints config-layer order (lowest precedence first), on/off state, and policy sources. Useful for diagnosing why the effective model differs from config.toml.
Override the configured model for the launched session (interactive or `codex exec`). Applies to this invocation only. Dedicated flag, preferred over `-c model=...`.
Generic key/value override; values parse as TOML, so the model string must be quoted twice (model='"gpt-5.4"'). Dot-notation supported. Highest-precedence layer at launch (alongside other CLI flags).
Switch to the local open-source provider; equivalent to `-c model_provider="oss"` and validates that Ollama is running. Selects `oss_provider` (`ollama` or `lmstudio`) when no provider is given.
Layers `$CODEX_HOME/profile-name.config.toml` on top of base user config; the profile file can set `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, and `model_catalog_json`.
Top-level key in ~/.codex/config.toml (or a profile / project / system layer). Sets the default model used at startup when no CLI flag overrides it.

Selects which provider serves the model. Built-in reserved IDs: `openai`, `ollama`, `lmstudio`, plus the built-in `amazon-bedrock`. Custom providers are defined under `[model_providers.<id>]` (base_url, env_key, wire_api, headers, auth). Note: `model_provider` and `model_providers` are ignored inside project-local .codex/config.toml for security.
Optional path to a JSON model catalog loaded on startup; a selected profile file can override it per-profile. Feeds the `/model` picker and `codex debug models`.
Model-behavior knobs rather than selectors, but part of the model-configuration surface. `model_reasoning_effort` is `minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh` (Responses API only; xhigh is model-dependent).

Scoped model overrides: `/review` uses `review_model` (else the session model); memory consolidation/extraction each take an optional model override; subagent roles load a per-role TOML config layer via `agents.<name>.config_file` which can set `model`.
The resolved model ID sent on each inference request after all selection layers apply. `wire_api = "responses"` is the only supported wire protocol now (Chat Completions API support is deprecated).

The catalog itself is enumerable as JSON via `codex debug models`; non-interactive `codex exec` streams the active model in its JSONL output. Not a selector, but the programmatic read path for the resolved/catalog model.
model_selection.site: codex debug models (JSON catalog) / codex exec JSONL `model` field

agent-models.precedence: interactive_command (/model, within an open session) > cli_flag (--model / -c / --oss / --profile) > config_file project (.codex/config.toml, walked root→cwd, closest wins, trusted projects only) > config_file profile (~/.codex/<name>.config.toml via --profile) > config_file user (~/.codex/config.toml) > config_file system (/etc/codex/config.toml on Unix) > built-in defaults. There is NO dedicated model-selection environment variable (unlike Claude Code's ANTHROPIC_MODEL): provider `env_key` vars carry API keys, not model choices. For security, project-local .codex/config.toml ignores model_provider, model_providers, and openai_base_url, so provider/model routing must come from user/system/profile layers or CLI flags.
agent-models.reason: Claudine's `model_catalog` module maintains a merged provider model catalog with static entries, alias resolution, and user overrides. The Codex lineup and selection surface have shifted and need a refresh: the current recommended set (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.3-codex-spark) and the deprecated models (gpt-5.2, gpt-5.3-codex); plus selection surfaces Claudine's Codex wrapper does not yet model — `codex debug models` as a programmatic JSON catalog source (a real dynamic `ModelCatalogSource`, unlike Claude Code which has none), `model_catalog_json` custom catalogs, the `--oss` / `oss_provider` local-provider path, config `--profile` layers, the catalog-driven `/fast` service tier, scoped model overrides (`review_model`, `memories.consolidation_model`/`memories.extract_model`, `agents.<name>.config_file`), and the `model_providers.<id>` custom-provider table (Responses-API-only `wire_api`). Claudine should also record that Codex uniquely lacks a model-selection environment variable. To merge/override and report Codex models accurately, the static catalog and the selection-surface model need updating.

local_runners.notes: Built-in lmstudio provider uses http://localhost:1234/v1 by default. The lms CLI must be installed and LM Studio must have been run at least once.

local_runners.notes: No native Codex provider. oMLX exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/* on port 8000. oMLX also ships omlx launch codex, which sets OPENAI_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY and execs Codex.
llama-server exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/* on port 8080 (build b7187+). The request model field is ignored in single-model mode; the server uses whatever model it was started with.
vLLM exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/* on port 8000. Each vLLM process hosts exactly one model; use --served-model-name aliases if needed.

Any local runner that exposes an OpenAI Responses API-compatible /v1/responses endpoint can be wired in as a custom provider. Runners that speak only the Anthropic Messages API require a translating gateway.

model-config.reason: Claudine's Codex wrapper and model catalog logic should account for first-class Ollama/LM Studio OSS providers, the experimental CODEX_OSS_BASE_URL/CODEX_OSS_PORT redirect env vars, and the fact that Codex's only user-extension API standard is OpenAI-compatible /v1/responses (not Anthropic). The exact local cache path for cloud-managed config/requirements was not verified.
Nested subagent child tool events were not verified as visible in the parent exec JSONL stream; source exposes collab state in parent events.

headless_constraints.constraint: No formal JSON Schema for exec JSONL.
headless_constraints.mitigation: Generate parser types from codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs or SDK TypeScript unions and preserve unknown events.
headless_constraints.notes: App-server schema is formal but broader and not identical to exec JSONL.

headless_constraints.constraint: Exec JSONL does not emit model, provider, auth kind, cwd, sandbox, approval policy, version, or MCP server inventory.
headless_constraints.mitigation: Wrapper should record invocation flags, selected config/profile, cwd, environment, and `codex --version` beside the stream.
headless_constraints.notes: OTel/app-server can expose richer metadata but is a separate integration.

headless_constraints.constraint: Interrupted turns may not produce turn.failed.
headless_constraints.mitigation: Treat process signal/non-zero exit and missing terminal event as cancellation/ambiguous failure.
headless_constraints.notes: Source marks interrupted turns as error_seen for exit status but the JSONL projector initiates shutdown without emitting turn.failed.

headless_constraints.constraint: Approval and user-input requests cannot be answered in exec mode.
headless_constraints.mitigation: Use approval_policy=never, preconfigure permissions, avoid prompt_tool-style workflows, and parse rejection messages as human-in-loop attempts.
headless_constraints.notes: MCP elicitation is auto-canceled; approval requests fail closed.

headless_constraints.constraint: Command output is aggregated.
headless_constraints.mitigation: Do not promise stdout/stderr separation for shell tools from exec JSONL.
headless_constraints.notes: Use app-server command execution deltas if separate streams are required.

headless_constraints.constraint: Project config and hooks load only when project is trusted.
headless_constraints.mitigation: For deterministic automation, use --ignore-user-config/--ignore-rules or explicit -c overrides, and record trust assumptions.
headless_constraints.notes: Project-local provider/auth redirection keys are ignored even when trusted.

io_contract.noise_handling: With --json, parse stdout line-by-line as JSON and keep stderr as diagnostics for startup/config/auth failures and non-zero exits. Without --json, stdout is final text and stderr is human progress.
io_contract.notes: The exec crate denies accidental stdout writes: default mode reserves stdout for final message, JSON mode reserves stdout for valid JSONL, and all other output goes to stderr.

output_formats.description: Progress is streamed to stderr and only the final agent message is printed to stdout.
output_formats.name: default text
output_formats.side_effects: Stdout is final text, not event telemetry; parser would lose session, tool, file-change, plan, and usage structure.

output_formats.description: One JSON object per stdout line with top-level type values including thread.started, turn.started, item.started, item.updated, item.completed, turn.completed, turn.failed, and error. Claudine should prefer this mode.
output_formats.name: exec JSONL
output_formats.side_effects: Stdout becomes parse-only JSONL. Final prose is represented as an agent_message item; -o can additionally copy it to a file.

output_formats.description: Alias used by the TypeScript SDK for the same exec JSONL mode.
output_formats.name: exec JSONL legacy alias
output_formats.side_effects: Equivalent to --json in the current CLI; prefer the stable --json spelling in wrappers.

output_formats.description: Writes the last assistant message to a file while preserving the selected stdout mode.
output_formats.name: final-message file
output_formats.side_effects: Additive output sink; useful for final artifacts but not live supervision.

output_formats.description: Requests that the final assistant response conform to a JSON Schema.
output_formats.name: schema-constrained final output
output_formats.side_effects: Constrains only the final agent message. It is not a schema for the JSONL event stream and can be combined with --json.

output_formats.description: Bidirectional JSON-RPC-like line protocol with method names, request ids, responses, and notifications.
output_formats.name: app-server stdio
output_formats.side_effects: Requires a client that initializes the server, starts threads/turns, handles server requests, and owns cancellation/lifecycle.

output_formats.description: Bidirectional JSON-RPC messages framed as WebSocket text frames.
output_formats.name: app-server websocket
output_formats.side_effects: Experimental and unsupported; must configure authentication before exposing beyond localhost.

output_formats.description: Single JSON object containing a tasks array and optional cursor.
output_formats.name: cloud list JSON
output_formats.side_effects: Applies only to cloud task listing, not local agent progress.

quirks: The stable user-facing flag is --json, but the TypeScript SDK still invokes --experimental-json as an alias.
thread.started.thread_id is the only session id in exec JSONL; there is no separate turn id.
Model reroute is not a typed model_fallback event; it is flattened into an item.type=error message.
File changes are summarized by path and add/delete/update kind only; no patch text is included.
MCP tool result uses structured_content in exec JSONL, while MCP protocol names the field structuredContent in some broader schemas.
Reasoning items contain summaries/text, not hidden reasoning.
JSONL item ids are synthesized by the exec projector and are not necessarily raw app-server item ids.
Without --json, stdout is intentionally only the final assistant message, which is good for pipes but poor for lifecycle supervision.
non-interactive-sessions.reason: Claudine runs structured Codex work over a managed app-server when every exec option maps exactly, projecting its notifications onto the exec JSONL events, and falls back to codex exec --json before submission otherwise.

schema_sources.notes: Best exact schema for codex exec --json; Rust Serde enum uses top-level #[serde(tag = "type")] and nested item.type values.
Authoritative projection layer from app-server notifications into the flattened exec JSONL stream.
Typed SDK union for exec stream events, generated or maintained from the Rust exec event types.
Typed SDK union for nested exec item payloads.
Official docs describe JSON Lines mode and list event/item families, but do not publish a complete exec JSON Schema.
App-server can generate JSON Schema and TypeScript bindings for its broader JSON-RPC protocol; useful context but not the exec JSONL schema.

session_metadata.auth: Not emitted in exec JSONL; auth failures appear as stderr/startup errors or error/turn.failed messages.
session_metadata.cwd: Not emitted in exec JSONL; effective cwd comes from wrapper invocation (--cd), config, or app-server/OTel surfaces.
session_metadata.mcp_servers: Not enumerated in exec JSONL; individual MCP calls expose item.server and item.tool.
session_metadata.model: Not emitted in exec JSONL; requested model is known from --model/config. Model reroute appears only as item.completed item.type=error text.
session_metadata.notes: The app-server protocol and OTel logs expose richer metadata, but the flattened exec JSONL stream is intentionally smaller.
session_metadata.permission_mode: Not emitted in exec JSONL; wrapper must record supplied --sandbox, --ask-for-approval, --yolo, and effective config if it needs this.
session_metadata.provider: Not emitted in exec JSONL; infer from config/model_provider or --oss.

session_metadata.version: Not emitted in exec JSONL; wrapper must capture `codex --version` separately if needed.

settlement.input_handling: Prompt is accepted during process startup; no separate acceptance receipt is exposed.
settlement.notes: Top-level error and stderr refine failure classification.
settlement.process_lifecycle: Exec is one-shot and exits after the turn.
settlement.settled_signal: terminal turn event followed by process exit

settlement.input_handling: A correlated JSON-RPC response establishes request handling, while notifications establish later execution.
settlement.notes: A steer accepted during a turn extends that same turn; an idle turn started by steering keeps the run open until it too completes.
settlement.process_lifecycle: The app-server remains alive after turn settlement and exits 0 when stdin closes; closing stdin during a turn abandons it (observed 0.157.1), so stdin closes only after settlement.
settlement.settled_signal: matching turn/completed, then thread/read reporting the thread idle with no turn started since

steering_mechanisms.notes: Activation remains a separate implementation decision; use the steering report's exact guards.
Activation remains a separate implementation decision; use the steering report's exact guards.
Activation remains a separate implementation decision; use the steering report's exact guards.

stream_contract.event_ordering: thread.started is first for a new thread; turn.started follows turn submission; item events stream during the turn; turn.completed or turn.failed is terminal for normal/failing turns. Interrupted turns may initiate shutdown without an exec JSON terminal event.
stream_contract.notes: item.started and item.completed for the same raw app-server item are mapped to the same flattened item.id while in progress. Assistant messages and reasoning are emitted as completed items, not token deltas.
stream_contract.unknown_event_policy: Skip unknown top-level or item types, preserve raw JSON for logs, and continue parsing by discriminator.

stream_events.notes: First event for a new thread; thread_id is the resume handle.
No turn id in exec JSONL.
Terminal success event for completed turns; usage is total token usage from the last token usage notification.
Terminal failure event when app-server marks the turn failed.
Unrecoverable stream error notification; process can continue until turn completion/failure.
Starts in-progress command_execution, mcp_tool_call, collab_tool_call, web_search, and todo_list items.
Currently important for todo_list plan updates.
Terminal item event for messages, reasoning, tools, file changes, errors, and final todo list.
Completed assistant message. The final answer is the last completed agent_message.
Reasoning summary text, not raw hidden reasoning.
Represents shell/command execution. Output is aggregated, not stdout/stderr-separated.
Emitted after patch success/failure; no per-hunk content.
MCP call start and completion are visible, including arguments and result/error payload.
Subagent orchestration tool. Nested child tool calls are not flattened into the parent stream unless surfaced as collab state/messages.
Search action is preserved from WebSearchAction when available.
Plan/todo state starts, updates, then completes at turn end.
Non-fatal warnings, config warnings, deprecation notices, and model reroute messages are flattened as error items.

subagents.notes: Subagents are enabled by default and only spawn when explicitly requested. Non-interactive approvals that cannot surface fail and report back to the parent workflow. Parent prompts can include non-interactive instructions for spawned agents.

tools.name: shell command / command_execution
tools.notes: Start is visible before execution completes. stdout/stderr are combined into aggregated_output.

tools.name: apply_patch / file_change
tools.notes: File changes are dedicated completed items after patch success/failure; no patch body or hunk details.

tools.name: MCP tools
tools.notes: MCP OAuth/login setup is outside the exec stream; configured required MCP startup failure exits with an error.

tools.name: web_search
tools.notes: Docs say web_search items appear in transcripts or codex exec --json output.

tools.name: todo_list / plan
tools.notes: Plan updates are item.updated events, then completed at turn end.

tools.name: collab_tool_call / subagents
tools.notes: Covers spawn_agent, send_input, wait, and close_agent orchestration.

unattended_requests.notes: Ordinary exec fails unavailable interactive requests rather than providing a general response channel.
unattended_requests.observed_behavior: The managed protocol sends server requests (command, file-change, and permission approval; request_user_input; MCP elicitation; dynamic tool calls; token refresh; attestation; current time). codex exec answers an MCP elicitation with a cancel action and every other request with JSON-RPC error -32000 (rust-v0.157.1).
unattended_requests.policy: Never fabricate approval or human input.
unattended_requests.request: tool approval, elicitation, or user-input request
unattended_requests.required_response: Answer as exec does: cancel an elicitation, refuse everything else; never approve. A request that cannot be read has no safe answer and fails the run as input_required.
unattended_requests.timeout_behavior: exec never leaves a request waiting; the managed client answers each at once.
